title: Russia and Ukraine hold peace talks in Istanbul
body:
On 29 March 2022 delegations from Russia and Ukraine met for talks in Istanbul, Turkey, hosted by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan. The Ukrainian delegation included Davyd Arakhamiya, Oleksiy Reznikov, Andrii Kostin, Rustem Umerov, Mykhailo Podoliak, Mykola Tochytskyi, Kyrylo Timoshenko, Oleksandr Kyrylenko and Oleksandr Chalyi. Vladimir Medinsky headed the Russian side and held a one-to-one meeting with the heads of delegations, with Arakhamiya taking part.

Erdogan addressed both delegations before the talks. He urged both sides to agree to a truce, saying, "Continuation of the conflict will not be good for anyone." He said continued fighting benefited no one, that each death and destroyed building cost the future, and that Turkey felt responsible for peace in the region. He expressed hope that the talks would produce a concrete result and said that successful talks in Istanbul could pave the way for a meeting between the Ukrainian and Russian leaders. After his speech he left the talks for Uzbekistan.

Russian businessman Roman Abramovich was also in Istanbul and held talks with Erdogan and delegation members before the negotiations began. The Istanbul round followed earlier meetings between the two sides, and it took place while Russian forces were still fighting around Kyiv, Chernihiv and Mariupol.
